narrative.overview:
The product reads like an inspection, not a sales sheet. It says what was examined, counts what it
found and names the cost before the step. It never says what any of that means, and it never says
*works*. The interface is a dark, neutral working surface of quiet layers: a Mica ground with a faint
lime tint, a tray, and every item pressed into its own cut-out. One lime marks what you can press and
where you are. The severities are tinted tags carrying a word and an icon. There is no success colour
at all: the best a check can say is *Checked*, drawn as a quiet dot.

Density sits between Default and Comfortable: a lot on the screen, held by the grid and the type
rather than by colour, as in Figma's panels. Edges come from hairlines before shadows, as in Linear.
Glass (acrylic) is the signature touch and is kept to the frame around a dialog or the Filters popover. Text never
sits on glass; it sits on an opaque sheet.

The components are **quiet and exact**: grey controls, hairline edges, states named by a word and a
shape, and colour held in reserve.
keyCharacteristics: Dark first; the light theme is designed, not inverted. One light slice exists, and the full theme comes in phase 09.
One brand colour, lime, which is never a verdict.
Every item in its own rounded cut-out inside a tray; auto-added items nest under their parent behind a dashed rule.
Findings are tinted capsules with an icon and a word: Problem and Note on the right of a row, `Conflict` beside the name.
Paths, refs, timings and file contents are in Geist Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Colour Is a Claim Rule
rules.body: A colour on screen asserts something. Lime asserts *you can act here* or *you are here*. Rose and amber assert a finding. Nothing else gets a hue.

rules.name: The No Success Rule
rules.body: There is no green anywhere. A passed check is a quiet neutral dot, because we examined the set and ran nothing.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on the step that removes. Inside a Problem the remove is a ghost button with rose text and a rose edge, filled only on hover; the solid red is kept for the confirmation.

rules.name: The Machine Reads Mono Rule
rules.body: If a string would be typed into a terminal or read by an agent, it is set in Geist Mono. Step numbers and durations also take tabular figures.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Rows, cards and panels carry no drop shadow. A shadow appears only where something is lifted over the place under it: the current place, a segment, a dialog.

rules.name: The Glass Frames, Never Holds Rule
rules.body: Acrylic is an 8 px lime-tinted translucent edge with no blur. It belongs only to the frame around a dialog or the Filters popover, and the sheet inside is always opaque. The Export mode has no frame. *Owner, 2026-10-19: kept like this for now. The blurred frame lives only on the phase-06 stand.*

dos: **Do** take every value from `06-concept/tokens.css` through `var()`. `tools/concept_ui.py --check` and the mockup build refuse a literal colour, px size or font name.
**Do** keep lime to what you can press and where you are, and keep one primary per screen.
**Do** pair a severity's colour with its icon and its word, as a tinted capsule or box.
**Do** draw *Checked* as the quiet neutral dot, and *Skipped* as `ban` with a dashed stage outline.
**Do** set paths, refs, timings, codes and file contents in Geist Mono.
**Do** put every item in its own cut-out, and nest auto-added items under their parent behind a dashed rule.
**Do** give every boxed object a visible edge; use hairlines before shadows.
**Do** measure every new colour pair with `tools/contrast.py`. AA applies to text, and 3:1 to a control's edge or a state mark. Today that is 88 pairs, all passing.
donts: **Don't** use a green tick, or any success colour. We examined the set; we ran nothing.
**Don't** use violet-blue neon, gradients or glow: the palette an AI produces for "AI tool".
**Don't** add `Verified` or `Popular` badges, stars, ratings, scores or cover cards. Usage facts are the only per-item evidence.
**Don't** put text on glass, or use glass outside the frame of a dialog or the Filters popover.
**Don't** draw a coloured ring round a row that carries a finding.
**Don't** use red for anything but removal, or lime for a verdict.
**Don't** let the browser draw a white checkbox or radio on the dark theme.
